01 — Brand Snapshotنبذة عن العلامة

Who Midfield is

Midfield Football Academy trains children aged 5–12 in Bahrain with a quality-over-quantity philosophy: capped groups of 14, two 90-minute sessions per week, and a curriculum built on technical, tactical, physical, and mental development. The brand must read as a modern, professional football club — never as a generic kids' activity center. Values lead the message: discipline, respect, teamwork, commitment.

5–12
Ages served — four launch groups: U5–U6, U7–U8, U9–U10, U11–U12
14
Max players per group — the core promise: individual attention
65
Phase 1 target — growing to 84 as groups split by age
2×90
Sessions weekly — 4:30–6:00 PM, Sat–Thu, Friday rest/match day

The official crest

Four sanctioned colorways of the club crest. Volt is the primary mark on dark grounds; black serves print on light grounds; white is the monochrome fallback. The gold crest is the ceremonial mark — reserved for certificates, awards, trophies, and premium touches, never mixed with volt in the same lockup.

03 — Typographyالخطوط

Two languages, one voice

Everything Midfield publishes is bilingual — Arabic RTL and English LTR, with equal care. The English display face is a tall condensed sans that matches the kit and flyer lettering; Arabic gets a heavy geometric that holds its own next to it, never a thin afterthought. All faces are free Google Fonts, so web, print, and the future system share one set.

Display — English · Anton

We build champions

Anton Regular · ALL CAPS · tracking +1% · line-height 0.92–1.05. Headlines, numbers, kit lettering, poster titles.
Display — Arabic · Cairo Black

نصنع جيل الأبطال

Cairo Black (900) · line-height 1.3–1.4 · RTL. Give Arabic display ~10% more line-height than Latin — ascenders and dots need air.

Instagram is the academy's primary channel. Every post runs through one of five content pillars and one of the templates below, so the feed reads as one club — consistent crest, consistent colors, consistent bilingual voice — under a single handle across all printed and digital materials.

Training Days

Joy

06 — Usage Rulesقواعد الاستخدام

Do & don't

Do

  • Use the new volt crest on every new material — profile pictures, flyers, kit, website, invoices.
  • Keep clear space around the crest equal to the height of the "M" in the wordmark.
  • Put volt on black or white only — it's an accent that strikes, not a wallpaper.
  • Write Arabic and English together, both native quality — never machine-translated, never one language shrunk.
  • Use the age-group color consistently: same color on the schedule, the wristband, and the parent portal.
  • State facts in mono-style labels: BHD 35 / month, due 28th, max 14 — exact numbers build trust.

Don't

  • Mix gold and volt in one lockup — gold is the ceremonial mark for awards and certificates; one metal per surface.
  • Set long paragraphs in volt or in Anton — both are display-only tools.
  • Post unbranded raw footage — every clip gets at least the crest watermark and end-card.
  • Use cartoon fonts, clip-art balls, or primary-color rainbows — Midfield is a club, not a kindergarten.
  • Show any child whose parents chose "I do not agree" on photo consent — the registration system tracks this; marketing must check it.
  • Stretch, recolor, outline, or add effects to the crest.
